description:
FILED s404 (Opus 5) during the rule-13 audit of every PPI workaround in the
tree against docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md.

`Pl::PExpr::_fix_ppi_ternary_label_bug` (PExpr.pm ~5808, called from
cleanup_for_parsing ~5636) exists because "PPI parses `word :` in a ternary as
a Label instead of Word + Operator".  On PPI 1.291 that does NOT reproduce —
six spellings all lex correctly (Word, Operator(:), Word):

    my $r = $c ? foo : bar;      $c ? foo : bar;        print $c ? foo : bar;
    f($c ? foo : bar);           $x = $c ? FOO : BAR;   $x = $c?foo:bar;

So either the trigger is narrower than the comment says (find it) or PPI fixed
it (drop the workaround).  Both outcomes need the same first step.

DO:
 1. find a shape that still produces a PPI::Token::Label in a ternary — try a
    ternary inside a hash constructor, after a fat comma, inside a heredoc-ish
    interpolation, and with a package-qualified word (Foo::bar :);
 2. if found: log it as its own ppi-upstream-bugs.md section with the dump,
    add the ppi-bug-report.t row and a canary keyed on it (that is what the
    rest of the workarounds now have);
 3. if NOT found: delete the workaround, with the usual bar — corpus-diff over
    both populations must be IDENTICAL (it should be a no-op if the trigger
    never fires), gate, and a canary row that goes RED if PPI ever regresses.

CONTEXT: the audit also logged three previously-undocumented PPI bugs whose
workarounds ARE live (§15 `)-1` negative-number split, §16 perl 5.40 `^^`,
§17 subscript-after-deref / KV-slice structure class), plus §14 (the readline
after a list operator).  This is the only workaround left whose bug could not
be reproduced.
subject: PPI ternary-label workaround may be OBSOLETE — find the shape or drop it
